question: At which 1815 battle did the Duke of Wellington defeat Napoleon?
romanUrdu: 1815 mein Duke of Wellington ne Napoleon ko kis jang mein shikast di?
explanation: Wellington defeated Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.3 A global power: Battle of Waterloo

question: Which flower is associated with Wales?
romanUrdu: Wales se kaunsa phool mansoob kiya jata hai?
explanation: The daffodil is a national emblem of Wales, alongside the leek.

sources.title: Visit Wales: national symbols of Wales
sources.locator: The daffodil and the leek as national symbols of Wales

question: What destroyed much of London in 1666 during the reign of Charles II?
romanUrdu: Charles II ke daur mein 1666 mein London ka bara hissa kis cheez ne tabah kiya?
explanation: The Great Fire of London broke out in 1666, the year after a major plague outbreak.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: Charles II and the Great Fire

question: How often are UK general elections normally held?
romanUrdu: UK ke aam intikhabat aam tor par kitne waqt baad hote hain?
explanation: MPs are elected at a general election, which is held at least every five years.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 5.6 The government: MPs are elected at a General Election

question: Which statement about Scottish and Northern Irish banknotes is correct?
romanUrdu: Scotland aur Northern Ireland ke banknotes ke bare mein kaunsa bayan durust hai?

choices.text: They are valid everywhere in the UK, but shops do not have to accept them
They are valid only in Scotland and Northern Ireland
They are not legal currency anywhere
They are issued by the Bank of England

explanation: Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own banknotes, which are valid throughout the UK. Shops and businesses do not have to accept them.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Which charity works to preserve important buildings, coastline and countryside in the UK?
romanUrdu: UK mein aham imaraatein, sahil aur dehat ko mehfooz rakhne ke liye kaunsi charity kaam karti hai?
explanation: The National Trust and the National Trust for Scotland are charities that preserve important buildings, coastline and countryside.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Does 'Great Britain' refer only to England, Scotland and Wales?
romanUrdu: Kya 'Great Britain' sirf England, Scotland aur Wales ko kaha jata hai?

choices.text: No, it includes the Republic of Ireland
No, it includes the Channel Islands

explanation: Great Britain refers only to England, Scotland and Wales, not to Northern Ireland.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Which tribal leader fought against the Roman occupation of Britain?
romanUrdu: Roman qabze ke khilaf kis qabeeli rehnuma ne jang ki?
explanation: Boudicca, queen of the Iceni, was one of the tribal leaders who fought against the Romans.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Who was voted the greatest Briton of all time in a 2002 public poll?
romanUrdu: 2002 ke awami poll mein sab se bara Briton kaun chuna gaya?
explanation: Winston Churchill was voted the greatest Briton of all time by the public in 2002.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Which TWO Houses form the UK Parliament? Select two.
romanUrdu: UK Parliament ke DO Houses kaunse hain?
explanation: Parliament consists of the House of Commons and the House of Lords.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: In which year did women gain the right to vote at the same age as men?
romanUrdu: Kis saal aurton ko mardon ki hi umar mein vote ka haq mila?
explanation: In 1928 women gained the vote at 21, the same age as men. The voting age for both was later reduced to 18 in 1969.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 5.2 The development of British democracy: 1928 and 1969

question: Who is the head of the Church of England?
romanUrdu: Church of England ka sarparast kaun hai?
explanation: The monarch is the head of the Church of England. The Archbishop of Canterbury is its spiritual leader.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: What kind of sporting event is the Grand National?
romanUrdu: Grand National kis qisam ka khel hai?
explanation: The Grand National is a famous horse race held at Aintree near Liverpool.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: What kind of work are Chaucer's Canterbury Tales?
romanUrdu: Chaucer ki Canterbury Tales kis qisam ki tehreer hain?
explanation: The Canterbury Tales are poems from the Middle Ages, one of the first books printed by William Caxton.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.2 Arts and culture: Chaucer; 3.5 The Middle Ages

question: When is Christmas Day celebrated?
romanUrdu: Christmas Day kab manaya jata hai?
explanation: Christmas Day is celebrated on 25 December.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Which group supported King Charles I during the English Civil War?
romanUrdu: English Civil War mein King Charles I ki himayat kis group ne ki?
explanation: Those who supported the king were called Cavaliers; their opponents were Roundheads.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: the Civil War

question: Which battle is commemorated in the Bayeux Tapestry?
romanUrdu: Bayeux Tapestry kis jang ki yaadgar hai?
explanation: The Bayeux Tapestry commemorates the Battle of Hastings and the Norman conquest.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Where was Anne Boleyn executed?
romanUrdu: Anne Boleyn ko kahan qatl kiya gaya?
explanation: Anne Boleyn, Henry VIII's second wife, was executed at the Tower of London.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: Henry VIII's wives

question: Which of these are examples of criminal offences?
romanUrdu: In mein se kaunse mujrimana jurm ki misalein hain?

choices.text: Racial crime and smoking in enclosed public places
Driving a car and paying tax
Joining a trade union and attending school

explanation: Racial crime and smoking in enclosed public places are given as examples of criminal offences.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: What type of character did Charlie Chaplin famously play?
romanUrdu: Charlie Chaplin mashhoor tor par kis qisam ka kirdar ada karte thay?
explanation: Charlie Chaplin became famous in silent films for his tramp character.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Must a person be at least 21 years old to stand as an MP?
romanUrdu: Kya MP ke liye khare hone ke liye kam az kam 21 saal ki umar zaroori hai?
explanation: The minimum age to stand as an MP is 18, not 21.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 5.5 Respecting the law: who can stand for public office

question: Who developed radar?
romanUrdu: Radar kis ne tayyar kiya?
explanation: Scotsman Sir Robert Watson-Watt developed radar, with the first successful test in 1935.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Where is the official home of the Prime Minister?
romanUrdu: Prime Minister ki sarkari rihaish kahan hai?
explanation: The official home of the Prime Minister is 10 Downing Street in central London.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition

question: Which TWO broadcast media must follow Ofcom's due-impartiality rules in election coverage? Select two.
romanUrdu: Intikhabati coverage mein kaunse DO broadcast media ko Ofcom ke due-impartiality rules follow karne hote hain?
explanation: Television and radio election coverage must meet due-impartiality requirements. This does not mean every view gets identical airtime.

sources.title: Ofcom: Due impartiality and due accuracy
sources.locator: Meaning of due impartiality; rules 5.1 and 5.5

sources.title: Ofcom: Elections and referendums
